script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saying the darkness showed up adds a sequence the passage does not give.
The cookie comparison makes the Light the subject of the joke. Comparisons must stay on the human side.
The passage says John testified so that everyone might believe through him; it does not describe an invitation being extended.
Saying John knew his job and stuck to it adds an unmarked claim about what he knew and how he carried out his role.
The comparison reverses the action: the world does not recognize the One through whom it was made, but the person in the joke walks past what they made.
Saying He stood right there adds a detail the passage does not give.
The passage says children of God, but does not say they are not hired hands or guests.
The claim that messengers appear elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
The passage says the children are born of God, not of human desire or will. It does not say here that nobody earns it.
The hat and apron joke makes the Son's glory the subject of humor.
Saying the Son is bigger than a prophet introduces a comparison the passage does not make.
The capital-letters line jokes about how Scripture is written.
Saying John is not trying to be the star adds an unmarked claim about his intentions.
Identifying David as Israel's king is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Identifying Elijah as a prophet of Israel is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
